cb_step_1.title: Select the CT volume
cb_step_1.simple: In the 'Input volume' section, choose the CT volume for this planning session.
cb_step_1.detailed: This is the preoperative CT scan of the fractured long bone (for example, femur or tibia). It is the foundation for all segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and reduction planning, so make sure it is the correct patient and side. Select the volume you want to process.

cb_step_2.title: Decide whether to crop to a region of interest
cb_step_2.simple: Decide if you want to crop the CT to a region of interest; if not, skip ahead to the segmentation steps.
cb_step_2.detailed: Cropping focuses the analysis on the fractured bone segment, reduces processing, and can make segmentation cleaner. If you check the 'Crop the input volume to an ROI' box, you will define the region in the next steps. If you do not need to crop, continue directly to creating the reference segmentation.

cb_step_3.title: Create an ROI for the long bone
cb_step_3.simple: In the Markups module, click 'ROI' to create an empty region-of-interest box named 'Longbone_Region'.
cb_step_3.detailed: The ROI will define the part of the CT that contains the fractured long bone. Keeping the processing window tightly around the bone helps the segmentation and reconstruction focus on the fracture. Create the ROI node; you will shape it in the next step.

cb_step_4.title: Enclose the fractured bone in the ROI
cb_step_4.simple: In the slice views, click and adjust the ROI box so it closely encloses the fractured long bone.
cb_step_4.detailed: The ROI should cover the whole fracture area including both the reference (fixed) and moving (displaced) fragments, while trimming away surrounding soft tissue and the opposite limb. A tight but complete ROI makes the later threshold-based segmentation faster and more accurate. Adjust the box in all three planes until the bone portion of interest is fully inside.

cb_step_5.title: Select the drawn ROI
cb_step_5.simple: In the 'ROI (Drawn in Markups)' section, choose the 'Longbone_Region' ROI.
cb_step_5.detailed: This tells the workflow which ROI represents the long-bone region you just drew. It ensures the crop operation acts on the correct box. Select the ROI you created.

cb_step_6.title: Confirm the crop
cb_step_6.detailed: This reslices the CT to the volume inside the ROI, producing a focused dataset of the fractured bone. Cropping removes irrelevant anatomy and makes the subsequent segmentation more reliable. After cropping, the workflow moves on to segmenting the bone fragments.

cb_step_7.title: Create the reference segmentation
cb_step_7.simple: In the Segment Editor, create a new segmentation named 'Reference_Segmentation'.
cb_step_7.detailed: This will hold the reference (fixed) bone fragment, the part of the bone that remains in its anatomic position. The reference fragment is the target that the displaced fragment will later be aligned to. Create the segmentation so you can add and threshold the reference segment in the next steps.

cb_step_8.title: Add the reference segment
cb_step_8.simple: Click 'Add' to create a segment, name it 'Reference_Segment', and set its color to Sage Green.
cb_step_8.detailed: The sage-green segment will represent the fixed reference fragment throughout the workflow. Giving it a distinct color makes it easy to tell the two fragments apart when you review the 3D model. Add and name the segment now.

cb_step_9.title: Open the threshold tool
cb_step_9.detailed: The threshold tool lets you select bone by its CT brightness, separating it from surrounding soft tissue. This is the first step of building the reference fragment mask. Open the tool to set the range.

cb_step_10.title: Set the reference threshold range
cb_step_10.simple: Adjust the threshold slider so the highlighted range covers the reference bone.
cb_step_10.detailed: Bone appears bright on CT while muscle, fat, and skin are darker. Set the range so the entire reference (fixed) bone fragment is highlighted without including soft tissue. A correct threshold makes the later island selection quick and the 3D reconstruction faithful.

cb_step_11.title: Apply the reference threshold
cb_step_11.simple: Click 'Apply' to generate the reference bone mask.
cb_step_11.detailed: Applying the threshold creates the initial segmentation of all bone-like voxels on the reference side. This raw mask usually also includes the displaced fragment and small noise, which you will clean up with the Islands tool next. Apply the threshold to proceed.

cb_step_12.title: Open the Islands tool
cb_step_12.detailed: The Islands tool separates the thresholded bone into connected components so you can keep only the fragment you want and discard the rest. This is how the reference mask is cleaned before reconstruction. Open the tool.

cb_step_13.title: Choose to keep one island
cb_step_13.detailed: With this option, clicking in the slice view will keep the connected bone island you select and remove everything else. This lets you isolate exactly the reference fragment. Select the option before clicking on the bone.

cb_step_14.title: Keep the reference fragment
cb_step_14.simple: In a slice view, click on the reference (fixed) bone fragment to keep it.
cb_step_14.detailed: Clicking the reference fragment tells the active tool to keep that connected island and discard the displaced fragment and any noise. This produces a clean mask of the fixed fragment, which will later serve as the registration target for the reduction. Click on the fragment that remains in anatomic position.

cb_step_15.title: Create the moving segmentation
cb_step_15.simple: In the Segment Editor, create a new segmentation named 'Moving_Segmentation'.
cb_step_15.detailed: This will hold the moving (displaced) bone fragment, the part that has shifted away from its anatomic position by the fracture. This fragment will later be repositioned during reduction planning. Create the segmentation to continue.

cb_step_16.title: Add the moving segment
cb_step_16.simple: Click 'Add' to create a segment, name it 'Moving_Segment', and set its color to Cyan.
cb_step_16.detailed: The cyan segment will represent the displaced fragment throughout the workflow. Its color keeps it visually distinct from the sage-green reference fragment. Add and name the segment now.

cb_step_17.title: Open the threshold tool
cb_step_17.detailed: As with the reference side, the threshold tool selects the displaced bone by its CT brightness. This is the first step of building the moving fragment mask. Open the tool to set the range.

cb_step_18.title: Set the moving threshold range
cb_step_18.simple: Adjust the threshold slider so the highlighted range covers the moving bone; the default should match Step 10.
cb_step_18.detailed: The displaced fragment has the same bone density as the reference fragment, so the default range is usually appropriate. Small adjustments may be needed if the fragment is thinner or has more artifact. Set the range so the moving bone is highlighted without including soft tissue.

cb_step_19.title: Apply the moving threshold
cb_step_19.simple: Click 'Apply' to generate the moving bone mask.
cb_step_19.detailed: Applying the threshold creates the initial mask of all bone-like voxels on the moving side. This raw mask will be cleaned with the Islands tool in the next steps. Apply the threshold to proceed.

cb_step_20.title: Open the Islands tool
cb_step_20.detailed: The Islands tool will isolate the displaced fragment from the rest of the thresholded bone. This is needed so the moving mask contains only the fragment to be repositioned. Open the tool.

cb_step_21.title: Choose to keep one island
cb_step_21.detailed: With this option, clicking in the slice view will keep only the connected bone island you select. This ensures the moving mask does not include the reference fragment. Select the option before clicking on the bone.

cb_step_22.title: Keep the moving fragment
cb_step_22.simple: In a slice view, click on the moving (displaced) bone fragment to keep it.
cb_step_22.detailed: Clicking the displaced fragment tells the active tool to keep that connected island and discard the reference fragment and any noise. This yields a clean mask of the fragment that will be repositioned during reduction planning. Click on the fragment that has shifted away from its normal position.

cb_step_23.title: Select the reference segmentation
cb_step_23.simple: In the 'Reference segmentation (fixed)' section, choose the reference segmentation.
cb_step_23.detailed: This identifies the fixed fragment as the registration target. The reduction workflow will align the moving fragment to this reference side. Select the segmentation you built for the reference fragment.

cb_step_24.title: Reconstruct the reference fragment in 3D
cb_step_24.detailed: This builds a 3D surface model of the fixed bone fragment from its segmentation. The 3D model lets you inspect the fracture surface and provides the geometric target for the registration. Click the button to create the reference model.

cb_step_25.title: Center the 3D view
cb_step_25.detailed: Centering the view frames both bone models in the 3D window, giving you a good overview of the fracture before fine adjustments. This makes it easier to orient yourself when the registration and planning steps run. Click 'Center view' to focus the scene.

cb_step_26.title: Select the moving segmentation
cb_step_26.simple: In the 'Moving segmentation (repositioned)' section, choose the moving segmentation.
cb_step_26.detailed: This identifies the displaced fragment as the part to be moved during reduction planning. The registration will then find how to reposition this fragment back to its anatomic location. Select the segmentation you built for the moving fragment.

cb_step_27.title: Reconstruct the moving fragment in 3D
cb_step_27.detailed: This builds a 3D surface model of the displaced bone fragment. Together with the reference model, it lets the workflow detect the fracture surfaces and plan the reduction. Click the button to create the moving model.

cb_step_28.title: Detect the fracture surfaces
cb_step_28.detailed: This identifies the opposing surfaces where the two fragments broke apart. These surfaces are the key anatomical landmarks for matching the displaced fragment back to its correct position. Click the button to run the detection.

cb_step_29.title: Initialize the registration
cb_step_29.detailed: This computes an initial transform that brings the moving fragment roughly into alignment with the reference fragment based on the detected fracture surfaces. A good initialization makes the final reduction planning more accurate. Click the button to start the alignment.

cb_step_30.title: Adjust the 3D view for inspection
cb_step_30.simple: Rotate, zoom, and pan the 3D view to get a clear angle on the fracture.
cb_step_30.detailed: This step only adjusts your viewpoint so you can inspect the reconstructed fragments and the fracture surfaces before planning the reduction. Rotate, zoom, and pan as needed to see the anatomy clearly. No clicking, placing, or marking is needed here; the reduction alignment is performed in the next step.

cb_step_31.title: Plan the reduction
cb_step_31.detailed: This computes the reduction plan, the rotation and displacement needed to return the moving fragment to its anatomic position against the reference fragment. The plan is the surgical guidance produced by this workflow. Click the button to generate it.
